name: WCIWF World Championship
epitaph: Twenty men entered the fed's own opening battle royal for this belt; Jumping Joey Smith outlasted the field, eliminating Barry the Bonecrusher last, to become the WCIWF's first-ever World Champion on its 24 November 1995 debut card, still champion when the surviving record breaks off a week later.

name: WCIWF US Championship
epitaph: An eight-man tournament ran the full length of the fed's debut card, but its own final between Mr. Wonderful and Harley Hatfield ended in a double count-out -- the belt still unclaimed when the surviving record breaks off, with a rematch billed for the following week's card.

name: WCIWF Television Championship
epitaph: The first match ever contested in WCIWF history opened this title's own eight-man tournament; The Great Oni won it in the final, defeating The Jet with a top-rope Savate From the Top on the fed's 24 November 1995 debut card, still champion when the surviving record breaks off.

name: WCIWF World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A seven-team elimination gauntlet on the fed's own debut card doubled as the deciding match for both this belt and the US Tag title; The British Battlers (Jumping Jack Jones and The Brown Bomber) were the last team standing, still champions when the surviving record breaks off.

name: WCIWF US Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Awarded under the same seven-team gauntlet's own dual-stakes stipulation as the World Tag title above: PAIN (Xtra Tuff and Everlasting Payne) were the last team eliminated before the final two, named the fed's first US Tag champions on its 24 November 1995 debut card, still champions when the surviving record breaks off.
